title: Church Discipline and Restoration
definition: Church Discipline and Restoration is the loving correction of sin in the Church for repentance, holiness, protection, and restoration.
summary: Biblical discipline seeks restoration, not humiliation.
christFocus: Jesus Christ loves His Church enough to correct, cleanse, and restore His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Church Discipline and Restoration teaches that Christ does not redeem people into isolation but into a gathered, accountable, worshiping, serving, and mission-shaped people. The Church belongs to Jesus, is formed by the Gospel, and is strengthened by the Word, prayer, ordinances, fellowship, and Spirit-empowered service.

This doctrine helps believers see the Church as more than a place to attend. It is the household of God, the body of Christ, and a visible witness to the grace, holiness, unity, and truth of the Lord.

The specific emphasis here is biblical discipline seeks restoration, not humiliation.. A healthy church life displays Christ's care for His people and His mission to the world.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because many people treat church as optional, consumer-driven, or disconnected from discipleship. Church Discipline and Restoration calls believers back to Christ's design for His people, where worship, truth, love, accountability, service, and mission are held together.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in church life with humility and faithfulness. Let church discipline and restoration move you to serve, forgive, gather, pray, give, submit to Scripture, care for others, and help the body of Christ grow in love and maturity.
